svg.text: claudia — Format ▸ Fonts…: the fonts of this document, and whether they are the ones it was written with, proposed
The same dialog in composes, computes and creates. Here: a composes document imported from report.docx, on Studio server. Any editor of the document may use it.
Beside Colours…: both are the document's look.
One line per family the document's styles ask for. Status in words and a sign, never by colour alone.
report · imported from report.docx · laid out with the fonts of Studio server
2 of 6 fonts are not as written: the footer (Segoe UI, missing) and endnotes (other version) may break differently.
the same file, from the server
the same file, from the server
the file kept in this document
Keep the fonts inside the document
Keeps the exact files of Fraunces, Inter and Source Serif 4 in the document (3.1 MB, sealed with it), so it looks the same on any Claudia
server, whatever fonts that server has. A font that may only stay on a server is named, never kept. Exports embed the kept fonts in .odt
and .docx where the font allows it.
In all three apps, beside Colours…, with Ctrl+Alt+E (free in all three;
Ctrl+Alt+F is Follow Computation in computes). The desktop clients'
native menus get the same entry.
What a person wants to know on opening this: does it look as it was
written, and if not, where. The sentence names the styles'
Since text has no direct formatting (D306), a font is always reached
through a style. A style's name opens Edit This Style.
Add font… puts a font into this document, not into the server (board
4C): no administrator needed. Replace… changes the font of every
style that names it, as one undoable command in the history.
The document records each family's file by SHA-256 (the planned
fonts.lock of E3.3). Other version: same family, different file; pages
may differ. Use this version re-pins it, as a logged command.
Kept fonts live in the sealed document like its images, so the server
adds them to the layout only for this document. Proposed default:
on, for every new or imported document.
